grades.quote: The TLB will be filled with two page table entries (page size is `16MB` ) without special software intervention.
grades.reason: Explains how a huge-page entry found during page walking (LDPTE) is split into two half-size entries when filled into the double-page TLB, with a concrete page-size example (16KB base, 32MB huge, 16MB TLB entries). It does not give the encoding of the page-size field or the huge-page flag.

grades.quote: Bit `6` of the directory entry is the huge page table entry flag bit, and `1` indicates that the directory entry actually stores the page table entry of a huge page at this time;
grades.reason: Covers how page walking recognizes huge-page mappings: bit 6 of the directory entry is the huge-page flag, the G bit moves, and the directory and page sizes are configured in PWCL/PWCH. It does not cover how page size is encoded in TLB entries.

grades.quote: When bit i is 1, it indicates that a page size of 2 i bytes is supported.
grades.reason: The PRCFG2 PSAVL field represents the TLB-supported page sizes as a bitmask, where bit i set means a page size of 2^i bytes is supported. This is a direct page-size representation in TLB-related state. It says nothing about page walking.

grades.quote: the configured page size is `2PS` bytes
grades.reason: Describes the TLB structure: STLB entries all share one configured page size (2^PS bytes) and MTLB supports a different page size per entry. This gives partial context on how page size is held in the TLB. It does not cover page walking or huge pages.
